---\nid: harness-gap-verifier-completion-verdict
+title: Verifier completion verdict
+status: ready
+---

# Verifier completion verdict

## Goal

Provide a bounded and revocable completion-decision entry point for the evidence
verifier. The entry point reuses `evaluateEvidenceVerifier`; it does not introduce a
second verifier authority or change product defaults, approvals, or locks.

## Contract

- `createCompletionVerdict` accepts a scope, task ID, evidence, and prior status.
- A task outside `scope.taskIds` returns `outcome: "out-of-scope"`, no record,
  and no transition.
- The existing verifier status is mapped exactly as follows:
  - `completed` -> `approved`
  - `insufficient_evidence` -> `insufficient-evidence`
  - every other status -> `rejected`
- Only `approved` returns a `node -> done` transition. All other verdicts return
  no transition.
- A verdict record contains only the task ID, verdict, evidence digest, finding
  codes, prior status, and the two explicit false capability flags. It never
  contains raw evidence.
- `revokeCompletionVerdict` accepts an approved record and returns
  `{ from: "done", to: priorStatus }`. It returns `null` for non-approved records.
- Every record explicitly sets `grantsPublish: false` and
  `grantsProductLock: false`.

## Determinism

The evidence digest is the digest returned by the existing verifier when
available. Otherwise it is SHA-256 over a deterministic serialization of the
evidence. Caller-owned evidence, scope, and prior-status values are not mutated.

## Safety boundary

This capability decides only the specified task's completion state. It grants no
publication, product-lock, release, approval, or default-setting permission.

id: s07-verifier-completion-verdict
+title: S07 verifier completion verdict closure
+status: closed
+---

+# S07 verifier completion verdict

## Implementation

`openclaw_runtime/src/runtime-core/verifier-completion-verdict.ts` adds the
restricted completion-decision API. It delegates evidence assessment to the
existing `evaluateEvidenceVerifier` and translates its status into one of three
completion verdicts.

The decision is bounded by the supplied task scope. An out-of-scope task has no
record and no state transition. Within scope, only an `approved` verdict emits a
transition from the recorded prior status to `done`.

The persisted decision shape is deliberately digest-only:

- `taskId`
- `verdict`
- `evidenceDigest`
- `findingCodes`
- `priorStatus`
- `grantsPublish: false`
- `grantsProductLock: false`

Raw evidence is neither copied into the record nor used to create a second
authorization layer. The prior status is retained solely to support bounded
revocation, which restores `done` to that status.

## Capability boundary

A completion verdict is not a publication grant, product-lock grant, release
permission, approval, or product-default mutation. The explicit false flags make
that boundary visible to callers and replay comparisons.

## Replay properties

For identical scoped evidence, the existing verifier result determines the same
verdict, digest, and finding codes. The implementation does not mutate inputs.
Non-approved decisions have no revocable completion and produce no transition.
